previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She presented with elevated liver enzymes and moderate ascites on ultrasound. Her white blood cell count rose to 17,700, prompting a workup that included a diagnostic paracentesis. Ascitic fluid analysis showed a white blood cell count of 132 with 5% polymorphonuclear cells, consistent with portal hypertension, and a positive culture for Bacillus species deemed a contaminant. CT imaging revealed cardiomegaly and mild pulmonary edema suggestive of diastolic heart failure, along with an indeterminate left adnexal density. She experienced recurrent hypoglycemia likely due to insulin stacking from recent shortened dialysis sessions. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, insulin regimen adjustment, and in-hospital hemodialysis. She was discharged home with stable condition, new insulin dosing, and follow-up plans including liver MRI and pelvic ultrasound.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with T1DM, ESRD on HD (___), HTN, 
multiple recent admissions for gastroparesis here with recurrent 
gastroparesis flare.

# Persistent Abdominal Pain: Patient presented to ED from 
hemodialysis with complaint of abdominal discomfort without 
associated nausea or emesis. Pain is same in quality as during 
her last admission (discharged ___. Stated she had been 
compliant with medications at home and is taking her insulin as 
directed. She only tolerated 80 minutes of her HD session on the 
day of admission before she stopped and presented to the ED for 
her abdominal pain. Abdomen distended but unchanged from last 
admission. During her last admission, RUQ ultrasound revealed 
evidence of moderate ascites and some hepatic congestion for 
which she received work up including CT Abd/Pelvis and 
diagnostic paracentesis. Repeat RUQ ultrasound on this admission 
was unchanged. Etiology of her abdominal pain is not entirely 
clear (absence of nausea/emesis is uncharacteristic of 
gastroparesis) but it was deemed suitable for workup as an 
outpatient.

# Incidental Adnexal Fullness: Left adnexal fullness seen on CT 
from last admission. Had recommended outpatient pelvic 
ultrasound in discharge paperwork, however the patient was 
unable to complete this in the short time between this admission 
and her last admission. Inpatient pelvic ultrasound on ___ 
revealed normal sonographic appearance of the bilateral ovaries.

# Transaminitis: Stable from prior values. Total bilirubin was 
normal. RUQ with signs of hepatic congestion and moderate 
ascites with gallbladder edema. Diagnostic paracentesis 
performed last admission on ___, with ascitic fluid analysis 
consistent with portal hypertension (SAAG > 1.1), 132 WBCs (5% 
polys). Ascitic fluid culture grew Bacillus species 
(non-anthracis) after several days which was felt to be a 
contaminant. She tested negative for Hepatitis A and B on 
___, and Hepatitis C on ___. Outpatient MRI liver is 
recommended to evaluate for regenerative nodular hyperplasia as 
a possible cause of her apparent portal hypertension and 
ascites, but this is not a likely explanation for her abdominal 
pain.

# IDDM: Difficult to control in the past. Hyperglycemic >500 on 
arrival most likely due to not receiving her scheduled insulin 
in the ED (was initially in 200s in ED). On floor, the insulin 
regimen was changed to that recommended by ___ at her last 
discharge (10u Lantus BID, 7u Humalog meal-time standing 
insulin, and correction ISS starting at 2u for 150-200mg/dL 
glucose and increasing by 2 units per 50mg/dL).

# Hyperkalemia (RESOLVED): Potassium 6.1 in the ED likely 
secondary to not receiving vast majority of her HD session she 
was scheduled for on day of admission. She received HD in the ED 
with post-HD electrolytes revealing K of 4.1.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ with abd pain and RUQ pain

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the liver and
gallbladder were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Liver gallbladder ultrasound study from ___, in
conjunction with CT abdomen pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

The hepatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. There is no intra or
extrahepatic biliary ductal dilation. The CBD measures 0.4 cm. The hepatic
veins and IVC are dilated. The portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. 
However, there is increased pulsatility of the portal vein on Doppler study,
and together with dilated hepatic veins and IVC, are suggestive of passive
hepatic congestion. Moderate ascites is again noted, not significantly changed
since prior CT study.

There is gallbladder wall edema, grossly unchanged compared to prior CT study.
This is a nonspecific finding which can be seen in setting of third spacing.
There are no other findings to suggest cholecystitis. There is no
cholelithiasis.

Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal limits

IMPRESSION: 

1. Gallbladder wall edema, similar to prior CT study from ___, and
this is a nonspecific finding which can be seen in the setting of third
spacing. There are no other findings to suggest cholecystitis. No
cholelithiasis.
2. Dilated IVC and hepatic veins, in conjunction with increased pulsatility of
portal venous flow, findings together suggestive of passive hepatic
congestion.
3.  Moderate ascites, grossly unchanged since prior CT study 6 days ago.
